name: Cable Seated Row
summary: A compound horizontal pull performed on a cable machine that targets the latissimus dorsi, middle trapezius, and rhomboids.

setup: Attach a close-grip V-bar handle to a low cable row station.
Sit on the bench, place your feet firmly on the footplates with a soft bend in your knees, and grasp the handle with a neutral grip.
Push back slightly to establish tension, sitting tall with an upright torso, shoulders back, and chest lifted.
steps: Initiate the pull by retracting your shoulder blades and driving your elbows straight back alongside your ribcage.
Pull the handle toward your lower abdomen or lower sternum until your elbows pass your torso.
Pause briefly while squeezing your back musculature.
Slowly extend your arms and allow your shoulder blades to protract slightly under control, returning to the starting position without rounding your lower back.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you pull the handle toward your body and inhale as you smoothly return to the starting position.
cues: Lead with your elbows, not your hands.
Keep your chest proud and ribs down.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at peak contraction.

common_faults.fault: Excessive torso swing using momentum to pull the weight.
common_faults.correction: Keep your torso nearly vertical and brace your core, moving only your arms and shoulder blades.

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the shoulders upward during the pull.
common_faults.correction: Keep your shoulders depressed down away from your ears throughout the movement.

common_faults.fault: Rounding the lumbar spine on the return.
common_faults.correction: Maintain neutral spinal alignment and keep your abdominal muscles braced throughout the entire range of motion.

precautions: Avoid locking out the knees aggressively on the footplates to reduce stress on the hamstrings and lower back.
